# Name the stylistic sets

SF Mono has two stylistic sets, and SF Mono Square has always carried them over: `ss03` draws `0`
without the slash and `ss04` draws `1` without the serif. Their names did not come along. The
glyphs are put together into a new font with `mergeFonts()`, which copies the lookups but leaves
the names behind, so apps that list stylistic sets (the Typography panel on macOS, Illustrator,
InDesign and so on) showed them as bare numbers or did not show them at all.

The names are now copied from SF Mono as they are.

| Feature | v3.5.2 | v3.5.3 |
|---|---|---|
| `ss03` | (none) | Alternate 0 no slash |
| `ss04` | (none) | Alternate 1 no serif |

This needs `font.style_set_names`, which FontForge added in 20251009
([fontforge/fontforge#5354](https://github.com/fontforge/fontforge/pull/5354)). The fontforge
formula in Homebrew is at that version already. Closes #100.

Turning the sets on works as before. A terminal or an editor asks for them by tag
(`font_features SFMonoSquare-Regular +ss03` for kitty, for example), and the names do not matter
there.

## Build

The build follows the Python fontforge is built for, instead of pinning `python@3.14`
(#148, #149). homebrew-core moved fontforge to `python@3.15` on 2026-10-14 and the build stopped
finding it. The CI fixes around it (#145, #146, #147) are in as well.

No glyph is added, moved or changed.
